visual.note: Industrial furniture: cabinet fronts and tops, wheeled base and tabletop caddy retain their intended floor or host contact.
Profile partitions face opposite sides; bench and round table sit on the floor; wall panel is attached to the back wall.
Floor vents and cable trays align with the floor grid in all shown directions.
Cable trays stay flat; four workstation directions expose the corresponding desk front.
Second desk family and console fronts align to their authored orientations.
Benches and workbench retain visible tops/base. Intake, bay and filter show honest unconfigured workflow warnings in this belt-free fixture.
Workflow machines remain visible beneath configuration warnings. Outbox and connector portal have continuous silhouettes and floor contact.
Dish and beacon use upright silhouettes; cabinet, safe and vault fronts remain readable.
Storage racks, shelves and server units are upright and grounded; no missing silhouettes.
Console bank mounts on the wall. Tactical table is compact at its 5x3 footprint; equipment bay is freestanding.
Deck perimeter markings are flat in all four rotations. Screens/holographic furniture preserve their low profile.
Display furniture, board and tank preserve top/front hierarchy. Dark display states are visible; no asset-loading errors.
Long displays and upright pylons keep consistent horizontal/vertical axes; intentional screen planes remain within their frames.
Fabricator, vat, easel and research equipment remain grounded; glass tubes retain their narrow upright silhouette.
Paper pile is hosted on a table. Thread rack, kiln and packbot retain their intended material and footprint.
Crates and racks preserve the approved scale reference; small boxes and parts bin are hosted on tables.
Communication and publishing props retain distinct readable silhouettes and bounded emissive areas.
Archive furniture and DJ booth retain top/front separation. Speaker is correctly mounted on its supporting table.
Couch, television, bar and arcade machines share the same room axes; couch base and back remain visible.
Bunk, pool table and vending/storage units remain proportional to the comparison chair; coffee machine rests on its host.
Plant is table-mounted; rugs are flat floor surfaces. Corrected nonblocking fixture permits actual passage.
Small and large rug directions remain flat and match their footprint orientation.
Floor light and intentional hologram are distinct from solid furniture; ladder, stool and chair retain floor contact.
Remaining chair directions expose the expected front/back; side and low tables retain low height.
Glass and diner tables have visible supports in both directions; guitar and booth remain upright.
Profile booths face opposing directions; diner chair fronts/backs agree with the four authored views.
Pod chair shells and openings agree with facing; low lounge tables remain low in both orientations.
Long tables preserve their authored legs; lamp and CRT pile sit on hosts; cable runs stay flat.
Cable runs and hazard markings follow the floor plane in every shown rotation.
Tall vegetation, terrarium and dispenser retain grounded bases. Holographic pet intentionally floats; plasma globe rests on table.
All six small tabletop objects are carried by their support tables, without visible isolated floor stickers.
Terminal and model ship rest on tables; vent is flat; fish tank, poker table and wooden bookshelf retain coherent depth.
Beanbag remains low; pinball and pods retain their bases. Opposing telescopes use matching tripod projections.
Camera and punchbag pairs face opposite directions; weapon racks are mounted to the back wall.
Opposing benchpress and recliner silhouettes align with the room axes; no new perspective mismatch seen.

limits: Interaction arrival is controlled using the real planners; it is not evidence that autonomous scheduling naturally chose every object. Walk traversal uses real ticks.
The seven wall-mounted rear paths are correctly outside the walkable floor and are explicitly excluded.
Workflow machines in catalog rooms are deliberately unconnected; this is not a new end-to-end backend workflow certification.
Study skins still lack some dedicated sit/walk artwork. Their complete animation set and every skin/pose combination are outside this pass.
Visual inspection covers every authored direction at room framing. Mirror geometry is checked mechanically; it is not 382 individual close-up art approvals.
Performance is a short local sample with one actor, DPR 1 and the CRT/lighting enabled. It is not a many-agent, multi-hour or multi-GPU benchmark.
Neither release controller was run; no merge, publish or release approval is claimed.
